verdict.rationale: Jev is a paid, per-token API, so user-set spending caps, budgets, or usage alerts are a fair question for it. The evidence shows only adjacent items: published per-token pricing, vendor-imposed rate limits that return 429, and per-response token usage fields. None of these is a user-configurable cap, budget, or alert that would stop a runaway workload.

support.subject: As a founder, I can set spending caps, budgets, or usage alerts so a runaway workload cannot generate an unbounded bill
